arms.name: spear
arms.title: spear
arms.reason: The image shows an iron spearhead with ribbed, leaf-shaped blade and long socket/tang, attributed by the museum to the Meru people of Kenya, consistent with traditional East African spear forms.

arms.name: arrow
arms.title: arrow
arms.reason: The image shows a complete composite arrow with a leaf-shaped iron blade, cane shaft, and leather binding, explicitly attributed to the Meru of Kenya, consistent with traditional arms of the region.

household.name: spoon
household.title: spoon
household.reason: A wooden spoon attributed by the museum to the Meru people of Kenya, consistent with traditional household utensils of the region.

household.name: väska, bag
household.title: väska, bag
household.reason: A triangular cowhide honey-carrying bag collected during an expedition to Kilimanjaro and Meru in the early 20th century — a functional leather container made and used in the region, consistent with Meru material culture.

photo.name: photographic print
photo.title: photographic print
photo.reason: Documentary photograph showing an M'Meru man from behind, with elaborate long plaited/ochred hair bound at the back, a cloth garment tied at the shoulder, and a spear over the other shoulder — consistent with traditional Meru male dress and adornment.

jewelry.name: öronprydnad
jewelry.title: öronprydnad
jewelry.reason: A round white-metal ear ornament with incised linear decoration and a brass chain fragment, collected in 1929 in Kenya and attributed to the Meru people of Mount Kenya's southern slopes; this matches known East African disc-form earrings worn by Meru/Kikuyu-related peoples.

jewelry.name: smycke, örhänge, jewellery
jewelry.title: smycke, örhänge, jewellery
jewelry.reason: The image shows an East African earring/ear ornament—a coiled metal ring supporting a beaded, ochre-clay-coated pendant—collected in Kenya and attributed to the Meru, close neighbours of the Akikuyu whose ornament style this resembles; such ornaments are plausible Meru wear.

jewelry.name: fingerring
jewelry.title: fingerring
jewelry.reason: The image shows a shield-shaped, arched finger ring in white metal with pierced double-line ornament along the edges — the museum's own description directly compares it to an original Meru example (Inv. 1911.8.2) and notes the Meru homeland, so this is a plausible, attributable piece of Meru jewelry.
